critiques.concern: The stat()-vs-exists() rationale and the companion "hardening" claim are interpreter-version-scoped, and were verified only on the non-canonical interpreter. The proposal states as fact that `Path.exists()` "swallows the ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EBADF/ELOOP family and re-raises everything else as a bare OSError," and that today an EACCES parent "escapes as an uncaught OSError" from `:387`. I confirmed both on 3.12.9 (a mode-000 parent makes `stat()`, `is_file()`, and `exists()` all raise PermissionError). But `pathlib`'s ignored-errno handling has changed across releases, the supported range is 3.11-3.13 (`doctrine/runtime-contract.md:56-60`), and the canonical gate interpreter is pinned at 3.13.13 (`gate_manifest.json` interpreter.version) — the proposal's own suite run was 3.12.9, and no 3.13 or 3.11 is available on this host. A Security Review cannot adjudicate a fail-closed disposition that may differ by supported minor version, and the claimed hardening may be a no-op on the interpreter the gates actually run.

critiques.concern: The proposal opens the resolver docstring to correct one overstatement and leaves a second one in the same sentence — one that is directly load-bearing for C1's ordering argument. Line :340 states the contract as "...with **no arguments / shell interpolation / relative segments**," but the only check is `interp.is_absolute()` at :380. I confirmed empirically that a path containing `..` is accepted today: `_resolve_interpreter` returned `('/Users/.../miniforge3/bin/../bin/python3.12', 'local-env.json')`. Since C1's placement argument leans on the symlink guard's priority, and `..` segments are the standard way an attacker reasons about lexical-prefix symlink walks (`_has_symlink_component` at :315-328 walks unnormalized components), leaving "no relative segments" standing as a stated contract while the code does not enforce it hands the Security Review a false spec for the exact guard they are being asked to rule on.

Enforcing is preferable: it also removes the residual question of whether `..` can defeat the lexical symlink walk, which the threat model currently does not address at all.

critiques.concern: The "no new execution path" argument is sound on capability but omits the compensating control the Security Review will immediately reach for. The claim rests on "`sys.executable` is the interpreter already executing the code that makes this decision, hence necessarily already trusted." That holds — but `templates/skills/_lib/lifecycle.py:1` carries `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, and `SECURITY.md:44-46` explicitly names a hijacked `PATH` substituting a shebang interpreter as a threat, prescribing `python scripts/x.py`, never `./scripts/x.py`. The shipped SKILL.md files do follow that (`templates/skills/session-start/SKILL.md:19`, `session-end/SKILL.md:19` both use `python tools/lifecycle.py`). The point of resolve-don't-bake is precisely that sub-tools should not inherit the ambient interpreter; after C1 a stale binding silently reverts them to it. The proposal asserts SECURITY.md "is not contradicted" without connecting these two facts, leaving the reviewer to reconstruct the argument.

numbered_critiques.concern: (a) The EACCES hardening claim is empirically FALSE, and the new test specified for it would fail. `_has_symlink_component` at `lifecycle.py:382` walks components via `cur.is_symlink()` (`:324`), which on 3.12 re-raises non-ignorable OSErrors. An unreadable-parent path therefore raises PermissionError BEFORE the proposed `stat()` probe ever runs, and it still escapes `main` (`:1270`) as an uncaught traceback. A C1-patched copy was built in the scratchpad and the EACCES case run against both the current tree and the patched copy: BOTH print `UNCAUGHT PermissionError`, and isolating the call shows `_has_symlink_component RAISED PermissionError at pathlib.py:840`. This falsifies four separate assertions: C1 property 2's "converts every other I/O failure into a proper LifecycleError (a small hardening this change carries)"; the edge-case line "Unreadable parent directory (EACCES) -> fatal LifecycleError (improved from an uncaught OSError)"; invariant (i)'s "and a new un-`stat`-able case"; and the new test `test_uninspectable_interpreter_path_refuses`. This is precisely the failure class that blocked the sibling proposal — a test plan asserting behavior the code does not have. (b) Independently, the stat()-vs-exists() rationale underneath that claim is interpreter-version-scoped and was verified only on the non-canonical interpreter. The proposal states as fact that `Path.exists()` "swallows the ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EBADF/ELOOP family and re-raises everything else as a bare OSError" and that today an EACCES parent "escapes as an uncaught OSError" from `:387`. Both were confirmed on 3.12.9 only; `pathlib`'s ignored-errno handling has changed across releases, the supported range is 3.11-3.13, and the canonical gate interpreter is pinned at 3.13.13. A Security Review cannot adjudicate a fail-closed disposition that may differ by supported minor version, and the claimed hardening may be a no-op on the interpreter the gates actually run.
